bounds.interruptedTurn: One admitted stream, one room, one original snapshot message, one ordered interrupted pair, one checkpoint, independent finalization, and one eviction after a successful checkpoint.
interruptedTurnLimitations: Cancelling the upstream reader synchronously stages the exact partial turn before capturing the checkpoint promise. Room release waits for the durable acknowledgement. Provider, billing and other finalization behavior are abstracted as independent success, failure or non-completion.

A failed checkpoint keeps this generation closed even if separate finalization succeeds. Restart from an unconfirmed checkpoint, applied-but-unacknowledged storage, incomplete chunk recovery, provider behavior and concurrent generation writes are outside the bound.

Eviction after a successful checkpoint clears the old generation. The real Workerd test runs the production Durable Object, controlled cancellation and failed finalization, and checks the complete ordered history before and after eviction. It does not drive a live provider, a failed storage transaction or canonical authorization.
bounds.mirrorRetirement: One non-Personal room with one due deadline, an initially clean or dirty snapshot, one subsequent version, one possible mirror rejection and fair alarm delivery. A due alarm can pause before snapshot selection or during its mirror. A local transaction removes the confirmed snapshot, replay claims and due deadline together.
mirrorRetirementLimitations: A deadline token abstracts the persisted time. A newer save may publish a replacement deadline or expose the replacement snapshot before its refresh. A version mismatch preserves that snapshot and gives it a full idle period.

A successful repository merge is the mirror acknowledgement. The Workerd test controls merge outcomes and advances stored deadlines for a retry. It uses the real scheduled alarm and SQLite storage. External Postgres availability, commit-reply loss, exact wall-clock delay, multiple queued snapshots, replay claim admission without a saved snapshot, tombstone cleanup and cache hydration remain outside this case.

assumptions: No fairness. One checkpoint transaction records the complete pair. This bound has no explicit history deletion.
Weak fairness of the checkpoint outcome and the room release continuation. The outcome can fail and keep the room closed. Finalization need not complete.
After one modeled eviction, weak fairness of successful loading from the original snapshot and acknowledged archive. Availability of that storage and a wall-clock deadline are not proved.
No fairness. A cancelled stream's checkpoint or room release continuation can remain pending.

Weak fairness of time reaching the current deadline, alarm delivery, snapshot selection, mirror reply and final transaction. The finite bound permits only one replacement save and at most one failed mirror. A surviving deadline eventually becomes due.
No fairness. Alarm delivery or the mirror reply can remain pending.
